cells.tense: You are staying near someone close to you, without moving to fix anything.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: With the person you're closest to, hold one quiet stretch this week without lifting it. No fixing, no deciding, no changing the subject. Let the stillness run its own length before either of you moves.
cells.core:
You and someone close have reached a settled place, and you aren't rushing it toward a result. That's why it holds without effort — the feeling has its own weight, and you're letting it sit rather than steering it. What alignment looks like when it's going well is close to this: two people near each other, nothing being fixed.

The easy move is to leave a calm stretch alone once it arrives. The growth here is to keep your seat in it past the first urge to tidy it up, and find out what the quiet has been carrying. Nobody needs a wise sentence from you. Going further down into what you already carry about this person is what turns a peaceful week into something solid to stand on.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting closeness sit still, and it holds.
cells.verb: Sitting with what the heart already knows before moving
cells.place: Where you feel with another rather than only about them

cells.tense: You will already be braced for how this closeness is going to turn out.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Name one ending from this past year, chosen or not. Keep a running tally of what it gave that you still have — a habit, a name, an object. Add to it whenever you notice one.
cells.core:
You're carrying a connection that hasn't asked anything of you yet, and you're already living past it — checking where it's headed, rehearsing how it may fail, adding weight that isn't here yet. What could be steady is being made restless by attention paid to a future you can't write into. You're leaning forward past today.

What brings you back is letting each ending you've already lived through yield what it grew instead of what it cost. Endings nobody chose still gave something, and going out to collect that is slower and more patient than the worry, which is why it settles you. You aren't being asked to stop minding what closed. Only to take the yield and set it somewhere you can see it.

cells.tense: You were standing beside someone and not fully arriving with them.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Think of one relationship you've drifted from. Bring what you think about them and what you feel about them into a single plain sentence on paper. Sit with the sentence a minute, then close the notebook and leave it.
cells.core:
You're near people and not quite with them — present but held back, close and unarrived. What's inside gets lived past instead of met. There's a version of the feeling already known to you, and it isn't being stepped into.

What helps isn't pushing harder at the closeness. It's lining up what you think about this connection with what you feel about it, so the two stop pulling apart. Start with one thread pulled straight out of the tangle, not the whole knot undone. A little of that lines up, and the difference shows in how you sit with someone before it shows in anything they say.

cells.tense: You are already keeping a room warm while filing it as nothing.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Somewhere this week, stay with one hard thing said between you and someone. Go back over it once more, slowly, before you close the subject. No verdict required.
cells.core:
You have a way of being with people that settles them — calm, unflustered, easy to be near — and it goes unmarked by you. You're not putting it on. Something in you is doing the work here, and the name you use for it leaves the doing out.

Next time, before you move, notice which part of the quiet is yours — see it plainly while it happens, then move or hold still. Authorship is only the difference between an act and knowing it was yours. Stay in the question until it stops shifting under you, and if no answer comes, that's a fine place to leave it.
